clue.text: Minimum probability one can get out of maze, roughly

indicators.note: the answer can be taken out of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Advice on the odds of finding your way out of a maze, which are close to nil.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits the two words the answer straddles, so the surface reads as a rough estimate rather than a string of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical sense: a probability of zero means an event cannot happen, the lowest value possible.

clue.text: Person risking money on form of Edward is beaten

parts.note: Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A gambler has put money on Edward's form, and Edward has lost.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. 'Form' looks like racing form but means a short form of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to better someone is to beat them, so the bettered side has been beaten.

clue.text: Calm about players including husband — it's randomly determined

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the calm word goes around the rest
to include is to hold within, so the players take in the husband

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm while a troupe that now includes a husband seems to be picked by chance.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the husband sits inside the players, and that whole group sits inside the calm word.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical sense: stochastic is the statistician's word for governed by random chance.

clue.text: Stake a lot — mostly that's nonprofessional

indicators.note: most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to lay a bet is to stake money

explanation.surface: Betting a fortune is the mark of an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonprofessional' reads as an adjective but works here as a noun: a nonprofessional, one who is not an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a layman is someone without professional training in a field.

clue.text: Within bounds of possibility, female having no difficulty ensnaring bachelor

explanation.surface: A woman easily snares a single man, within the bounds of what is possible.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside EASILY as EASI(B)LY, and F goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasibly means in a way that is possible or can be done.

clue.text: Accomplished what's likely after 24 down

definitions.note: the second definition is the part of PROBABLE that follows PROB

definitions.meaning: the tail of a word for likely, once 24 down's letters stand in front

explanation.surface: Someone skilled does whatever tends to follow a problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 24 down is PROB; put ABLE after it and you get PROBABLE, 'likely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for skilled, and the ending that turns PROB into PROBABLE.

clue.text: Place for gambling in which cash is not always endless

indicators.note: every one of the three words loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A gambling house where your money does not last for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not always endless' sounds like a warning about your cash running out; in fact 'always' tells you all three words are cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word came from Italian for a little house, later a house for gaming.

clue.text: Probability of dice delivering six initially

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A question about the chance of rolling a six.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the chance of rolling a six is exactly what the odds are.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: the odds of a six are the probability of rolling one.

clue.text: Chance to happen, as you announced in gallery, on drawing

parts.note: a drawn game leaves the scores even

indicators.note: 'in' places the sound of 'you' inside the gallery's name, as a visitor stands in a gallery

parts.note: the letter U is said like 'you'

explanation.surface: Something happens in a gallery just as you said it would, over a drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' and 'gallery' together paint a picture of art; here drawing means a tied game. The Tate is a group of London art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to eventuate is to come to pass, and a chance event is one that may come to pass.

clue.text: Location for dicey games lacking excitement, we hear

indicators.note: the answer is how the word is said, not spelt

explanation.surface: A place where dice games are played, which sounds rather dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicey' plays on dice: board games such as backgammon are played with dice.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by example: backgammon and ludo are dice games played on a board.

clue.text: Probability in relating to one sense organ — or another

parts.note: otic = relating to another sense organ, the ear
p is the symbol for probability

explanation.surface: Some chance that we are talking about one sense organ or a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or another' is itself wordplay: the word for another sense organ, OTIC, takes P to become O(P)TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: optic means relating to the eye or vision.

clue.text: Origin of theme in Brendan's collection — they can be hard to solve

definitions.text: they can be hard to solve

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

parts.note: the setter Brendan speaking of himself

explanation.surface: The setter points to where this puzzle's theme began in his own set of crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter referring to himself by name means ME or MY; here the possessive gives MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by example: detective mysteries, and crosswords like this one, are puzzles set to be solved.

clue.text: Associated with probability one can tire when wrecked

indicators.note: the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A probability claim that you can get tired when shattered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' belongs to the definition: an event with probability one is certain. The surface reads it as 'one can', a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical sense: probability theory gives the value one to an outcome sure to happen.

clue.text: Like simple random number generator, sugar?

definitions.text: Like simple random number generator, sugar?

parts.note: the surface suggests software; the simplest generator of random numbers is a die
sugar is sold in lumps of the same shape as a die

explanation.surface: A question about what a die and a lump of sugar have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Random number generator' sounds like software; the simplest one is a die, which is a cube, like a sugar lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a die and a sugar lump are cube-shaped, that is, cubic.

clue.text: Bet on way of escaping and withdraw

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
an out = a way of escape

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on a way out, then pulls out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bet on' looks like the start of a wager; BACK is the gambling verb for supporting a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: backing out is pulling out of a deal or plan already agreed.

clue.text: Perfectly played in part of church, with female ending

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: Music played flawlessly in a church, finishing with a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanceless is a cricket word: an innings in which the batter gave the fielders no chance to get them out.
explanation.definitionFit: A chanceless innings is one played without a single mistake.

clue.text: Betting system's takes

definitions.note: the first definition reads as TOTE'S, a possessive
definitions.meaning: the Tote, short for totalizator, with 's
to tote = to carry, take along

explanation.surface: What a betting operation takes in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tote is a British pool betting system, so 'betting system's' is TOTE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: The tote is a betting system, and to tote is to carry or take.

clue.text: Wager I had placed inside — it helps one clean up

indicators.note: 'placed inside' describes putting one thing into another, so I'D goes into the wager

explanation.surface: A gambler describes placing a bet that helps them clean up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clean up' looks like a gambler's big win; it means washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by function: a bidet is a low basin for washing oneself.

clue.text: Not enough, as cash — toss for it

definitions.meaning: short of a required sum by some amount
to fling or throw, as at a fairground stall

explanation.surface: Short of money, so decide by tossing a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A shy is a throw, as in a coconut shy, a fairground game of throwing balls at coconuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Five dollars shy means five dollars short; to shy something is to toss it.

clue.text: Contract overturned in random long-term plan

parts.note: a stray shot is a random one

indicators.note: 'in' means within, so the reversed word sits within the word for random

parts.note: to contract an illness is to get it

explanation.surface: A contract gets torn up inside some haphazard long-range plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a legal agreement, a noun; the wordplay needs the verb, as in contracting a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a strategy is the overall long-range plan, as opposed to short-term tactics.

clue.text: A non-English type in English course that offers better opportunities

definitions.text: English course that offers better opportunities

parts.note: a native of the country north of England

explanation.surface: An outsider on an English course looking for better chances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is one who bets: Ascot is an English racecourse, so it offers bettors their chances.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, England, where punters bet on horses.

clue.text: Approach counter in gaming club and drink

explanation.surface: Walk up to the counter at a gambling club and order a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Approach' reads as a verb; it is the golf noun, a short shot onto the green. 'Club' also nods to golf.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a chip shot is a short, lofted approach to the green.

clue.text: Poet having change of heart is opportunist

indicators.note: the middle letter of the poet's name is swapped for another

explanation.surface: A poet who changes his mind is only out for himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' is the middle letter of CHAUCER; swap U for N. A chancer is British slang for someone who takes chances for gain.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is an opportunist who tries their luck.

clue.text: A wrong card, bridge player concludes, for game situation

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters of card are disordered

parts.note: East, one of the four players at bridge

explanation.surface: A card game goes wrong and a bridge player finishes the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named for compass points, so 'bridge player' is N, S, E or W; here East.
explanation.definitionFit: An amusement arcade is where games are sited.

clue.text: Diplomacy's about constant plans to reduce risk

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so TACT IS goes around the constant

parts.note: c, the speed of light, a physical constant

explanation.surface: Being diplomatic is about steady plans to keep risk down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diplomacy's' must be read as 'diplomacy is', TACT IS, not as a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are planned moves to gain an advantage or limit risk.

clue.text: Decisively raised a little bit of money — wasn't easy

definitions.text: Decisively raised a little bit of money
definitions.meaning: a coin flipped into the air to settle a decision
was restless, turning over and over in bed

explanation.surface: Someone raised a small sum decisively, and it was hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a coin toss, flipping a coin up to settle a question; the second is tossing and turning, a restless night.
explanation.definitionFit: Tossing a coin sends it up to decide; one who tossed all night was uneasy.

clue.text: Embezzles or gambles after initial loss

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone either steals funds or gambles after losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial loss' sounds like losing a stake at the start; it means losing the initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To peculate is to embezzle money entrusted to you.

clue.text: A little difficulty? Before 6, it's to be expected

definitions.note: the second definition is the part of PROBABLE that comes before ABLE

definitions.meaning: the front of a word for likely, once 6 down's letters follow

explanation.surface: A minor snag, which is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: PROB is a shortened 'problem', which is why the difficulty is 'little'. Put it before 6 down, ABLE, and you have PROBABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Prob is informal shorthand for problem, as in 'no prob'.

clue.text: Something drawn using paper a great deal?

definitions.meaning: slips of paper drawn from a hat to decide by chance

explanation.surface: A question about what gets drawn with lots of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' looks like sketching; lots are drawn from a hat on slips of paper to choose at random.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing lots settles a choice by chance; lots also means a great deal.

clue.text: Player out of luck, perhaps? Not so far losing head

indicators.note: to lose the head is to lose the top, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: An unlucky gambler who hasn't got far and has lost his cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' sounds like a gambler losing his temper; it takes the first letter off CLOSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A player whose luck has run out ends up the loser.

clue.text: Playboy that takes in money at roulette table

definitions.text: that takes in money at roulette table
definitions.meaning: the croupier's long-handled tool for gathering chips

explanation.surface: A playboy scooping up money at a roulette table.
explanation.walkthrough: A croupier gathers chips with a long-handled rake; a rake is also a dissolute man about town.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a pleasure-seeking playboy, and also the croupier's tool for gathering stakes.

clue.text: Uncertain news from France I don't broadcast

indicators.note: the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A French rumour that someone refuses to spread.
explanation.walkthrough: On-dit is French for 'they say', borrowed into English for a piece of hearsay.
explanation.definitionFit: An on-dit is a rumour or piece of gossip, news of doubtful truth.

clue.text: Company losing little time before a week-end? It has some chance of success

definitions.text: It has some chance of success

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it

parts.note: an end of WEEK is W or K

explanation.surface: Visitors stay a little less long before the end of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A week-end' is not Saturday and Sunday: it is one end of the word WEEK, which is W OR K, spelt out as WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: Defined by description: guesswork is estimating without full facts, so it may or may not be right.
